task: Phase E Track B5 (acquire more corpora), source group b: Aider benchmark logs, Terminal-Bench traces and run artifacts, METR public task-suite transcripts and released logs. Includes internal-embodiment prior-art checks of the same systems.
scope_note: Public corpora only. Nothing related to the local Qwen swarm was read or run. No agent transcripts were generated, and no downloaded code was executed. The only code run was the scripts in analysis/out/phase_e/track_b/B5b_aider_tbench_metr/. Gated sets were not downloaded: only their public dataset cards were read.
bottom_line: DOWNLOADED (passed the field audit): (1) terminal-bench-2-leaderboard, a 4.762 GB field-audited subset of the official Terminal-Bench 2.0 leaderboard submissions (HF harborframework/terminal-bench-2-leaderboard @572b2614, apache-2.0 in the card). It holds 75 agent/model submissions, 32,803 trials, 9,670 ATIF trajectories with 399,962 timestamped steps and 472,285 tool calls, 1,379 native Claude Code session JSONLs, 884 native Gemini-CLI logs, 443 hookele logs and 1,332 asciinema casts. (2) glm52-nf3-tb21-traces, 89 MB, 85 Terminus-2 trials on TB 2.1 with a self-hosted GLM-5.2 (HF 0xSero/..., mit in the card).

REQUEST-ID COVERAGE (B4 column): a second public corpus carries Anthropic provider request ids. The WozCode__Claude-Opus-4.6 submission in the TB2 subset has 444/444 sessions with requestId, 7,272 distinct ids and 12,327 carrying entries. 12,327/12,327 decode as UUIDv7, and 12,279/12,327 (0.9961) fall within [-2 s, +600 s] of the carrying entry. Event-minus-id is p50 4.2 s, p95 46 s and minimum +0.548 s. Same harness (Claude Code 2.1.86, entrypoint sdk-cli) and provider as swechat, but a different operator, period (Mar 2026) and task suite. It adds coverage, not harness diversity.

NEW PROVIDER CLOCK (OpenAI, 1 s resolution): hookele__gpt5.1-codex-mini has 12,804 OpenAI Responses resp_ ids, all in the hex50 layout (16-hex prefix, '00', 8-hex unix seconds; per B2a, undocumented). 12,804/12,804 decode to a second inside [harness llm_call ts - 1 s, harness stream_summary ts + 1 s]. This is a cross-provider replication of the id-clock bracket idea at 1 s granularity.

HARNESS TIMERS: 4,876 Terminus-family trials (Terminus-2, Terminus-KIRA, Meta-Harness, AfterQuery) carry result.json agent_result.metadata.api_request_times_msec. These are 146,857 harness-measured wall times, one per LLM request, from time.time() around chat.chat in harbor terminus_2.py. Combined with step timestamps minted on the host after command execution, they allow a per-step split of LLM time versus execution plus wait time. That is directly usable for N1 and N3. Caveat: Terminus waits an agent-chosen 'duration' per keystroke batch, so execution time is partly model-controlled.

FAILED THE FIELD AUDIT or NOT PUBLIC: Aider benchmark logs. The artifacts are per-exercise .aider.results.json aggregates and a markdown chat history with only a session-start timestamp; there are no tool calls or call/result join, and no run directories are published. METR report transcripts are embedded excerpts only. METR time-horizon runs.jsonl is per-run aggregates with no licence. yoonholee/terminalbench-trajectories reduces steps to {src,msg,tools,obs} with no per-step timestamps. mercor ApexAgents TB2.1 traces have no per-message timestamps.

LISTED FOR A HUMAN (not downloaded): METR MALT (gated by a contact-info agreement; MIT). The card schema passes on paper: per-node first_called_at int64, a parent-pointer DAG and function_call nodes. This account's HF token already has access, so a human only needs to approve downloading the default config of malt-transcripts-public (1.66 GB). Also listed: TB 2.1 official leaderboard jobs on Harbor Hub (needs the harbor CLI, i.e. executing third-party code; per-job licence not stated), several unlicensed TB trace dumps on HF, and Simple-Codex codex.txt (OpenAI resp_ ids plus per-exec 'Wall time').

PRIOR-ART INTERNAL CHECK: Harbor's ATIF model already enforces referential call/result integrity at write and load time. It checks that each observation source_call_id is in the same step's tool_call_ids, that step_ids are sequential and that timestamps are ISO-8601 parseable. Structural join checking is therefore PARTIAL/TAKEN as schema validation. Nothing in Harbor, Terminal-Bench, Aider or METR's released material checks timing, provider-id clocks, or result-content consistency to detect fabricated tool output. TB's integrity policy relies on static config checks plus an LLM 'agent judge'.

downloads.acquired_total_note: Shared directory; other B5 agents downloaded concurrently. The total was checked before each download and stayed under 25 GB.
downloads.cap_issue: terminal-bench-2-leaderboard content is 4.762 GB, under the 5 GB per-corpus cap. On disk it is 5.884 GB because hf_repo/.git holds 1.070 GB: 0.470 GB real packs, 0.110 GB index, and a 0.476 GB orphaned .tmp pack from a killed git auto-gc. Nothing was deleted (append-only rule). HUMAN DECISION: hf_repo/.git can be removed safely, because the content is covered by _acquisition/FILES_SHA256.v2_lf_exact.jsonl.
incidents: Per-file HTTPS download hit the account-wide HF quota of 5000 resolver requests per 5 minutes ('We had to rate limit you, you hit the quota of 5000 resolvers requests per 5 minutes period'), which other agents share. I stopped after 1,766 files and switched to a git partial clone with sparse-checkout plus the LFS batch API, which uses no resolver quota.

Global git core.autocrlf=true converted LF->CRLF in 48,185 (TB2) and 788 (GLM) text files at checkout. fix_crlf.py restored the exact committed blob bytes and core.autocrlf was set false locally. Verified: 1,766/1,766 files identical to the raw HTTPS bytes, and the TB2 content total equals the HF listing (4,762,210,223 bytes). The census was re-run after the restore and is unchanged.

A 'git lfs ls-files' I ran in the blob:none partial clone spawned 'git ls-tree -r -l', which triggered lazy blob fetches of the whole 40 GB repo from 02:22 to 02:34 local time. TaskStop did not kill the git grandchildren; I killed them with taskkill. About 0.03 GB of stray blobs landed in .git, plus the 0.476 GB orphaned gc temp pack. remote.origin.url was then set to https://invalid.invalid/lazy-fetch-blocked to prevent a recurrence; the original URL is recorded in ACQUISITION.json.

field_audit.method: Median-size agent/trajectory.json from each of the 25 ATIF-bearing submissions (atif_audit.json), plus one sample of each native log type. The full census after download is in tb2_stats_v2.json and id_clock_checks.json.
field_audit.pass_detail: ATIF: every step has an ISO-8601 timestamp (399,962/399,962). Resolution is microseconds (6 digits) for Terminus-family, Judy, Deep-Agents, NexAU and Simple-Codex; milliseconds (3 digits) for Claude Code-derived, Gemini-CLI, JJAgent and Wecode; nanosecond-precision strings for vix. Join: 173,384 of 317,403 observation results join by source_call_id (Claude Code, Gemini-CLI, Judy, JJAgent, Deep-Agents, NexAU, Simple-Codex, Wecode, vix). The other 144,019 are Terminus-family, where all keystroke tool_calls of a step map to one terminal observation in the same step object: strict step-level pairing, not per-call. Native Claude Code: 155,051 entries, 153,567 with ms timestamps, 47,939 tool_use with 47,852 joined to tool_result by tool_use_id. Gemini-CLI: 21,009/21,009 tool calls with their own ms timestamp and an id-joined functionResponse. hookele: 12,230/12,230 tool_execution rows with call_id, at 1 s resolution.

schema_note.layout: submissions/terminal-bench/2.0/<agent>__<model>/{metadata.yaml, <job>/{config.json, result.json, job.log?, <task>__<trial>/{result.json, exception.txt?, agent/{trajectory.json?, recording.cast?, sessions/projects/-app/<uuid>.jsonl?, gemini-cli.trajectory.json?, .hookele/traj.jsonl?}}}}
schema_note.result.json (trial): id, task_name, trial_name, config{agent{name,model_name,kwargs},environment{type},timeout_multiplier}, agent_info{name,version,model_info{name,provider}}, agent_result{n_input_tokens,n_cache_tokens,n_output_tokens,cost_usd,metadata{n_episodes, api_request_times_msec[] (Terminus family), summarization_count}}, verifier_result.rewards.reward, exception_info, started_at/finished_at plus environment_setup/agent_setup/agent_execution/verifier {started_at,finished_at} (ISO-8601 microsecond Z). 32,803 trials; 32,178 with an agent_execution window; 5,398 with exception_info.
schema_note.ATIF trajectory.json (harbor src/harbor/: schema_version (v1.2: 889, v1.5: 4,879, v1.6: 3,902 files), session_id, agent{name,version,model_name}, steps[{step_id, timestamp (ISO-8601), source system|user|agent, model_name, message, reasoning_content, tool_calls[{tool_call_id,function_name,arguments}], observation{results[{source_call_id,content}]}, metrics{prompt_tokens,completion_tokens,cached_tokens,cost_usd,logprobs,...}, extra}], final_metrics. Terminus-2 mints the step timestamp with datetime.now() on the host after executing the step's commands (terminus_2.py ~l.1630). 567 files have non-monotonic step timestamps (JJAgent 462, WozCode 105), likely subagent or sidechain interleaving. Treat this as a loader caveat, not a signal.
schema_note.native Claude Code JSONL: Same format as cc_local and swechat raw: type user|assistant|queue-operation|progress..., uuid, parentUuid, sessionId, timestamp (ms Z), version, message{id,model,content[tool_use{id,name,input}|tool_result{tool_use_id,content,is_error}],usage}, toolUseResult{stdout,stderr,interrupted,...}, requestId (WozCode only), sourceToolAssistantUUID. Large tool outputs are spilled to sessions/projects/-app/<uuid>/tool-results/*.txt, which were NOT downloaded.
schema_note.gemini-cli.trajectory.json: sessionId, startTime, lastUpdated, messages[{id, timestamp (ms Z), type user|gemini, content, thoughts, tokens{input,output,cached,thoughts,tool,total}, model, toolCalls[{id, name, args, result[{functionResponse{id,name,response{output}}}], status, timestamp}]}]. Shell outputs embed 'Exit Code: N'.
schema_note.hookele .hookele/traj.jsonl: type start|llm_call|stream_summary|raw_response|tool_execution|plan_update..., ts (ISO-8601, 1 s), iteration, response_id (OpenAI resp_), usage{input_tokens,output_tokens,cached_tokens,reasoning_tokens}, call_id, name, args, output.
schema_note.recording.cast: asciinema v2: header {version,width,height,timestamp (unix s),env}, then [rel_seconds (us), 'i'|'o', data] events. 1,332 casts, 2,770,960 events. A terminal-level stream with its own clock, independent of the ATIF step clock. Where asciinema runs (inside or outside the sandbox) is UNVERIFIED, so its trust level under the threat model is open.

corpora.sessions: 32,803 trials (75 submissions). Structured per-event logs: 9,670 ATIF, 1,379 Claude Code JSONL (1,325 sessions), 884 Gemini-CLI, 443 hookele
corpora.tool_calls: ATIF 472,285; Claude Code tool_use 47,939; Gemini-CLI 21,009; hookele 12,230
corpora.ms_timestamps: YES. Per step/entry ISO-8601 at us (Terminus family etc.) or ms (Claude Code, Gemini-CLI, JJAgent, Wecode) resolution; hookele at 1 s; asciinema casts at us relative to a unix-second header.
corpora.call_result_join: YES. ID join for 173,384 ATIF observations, 47,852 Claude Code and 21,009 Gemini-CLI pairs. Terminus family (144,019 observations) uses step-level strict pairing (calls and observation co-located in one step object), not per call.
corpora.token_counts: YES. ATIF step metrics on 253,556 steps; Claude Code message.usage; Gemini tokens per message; hookele usage; trial totals in result.json.
corpora.truncation_markers: Terminus-2 observations carry '[... output limited to 10000 bytes; N interior bytes omitted ...]' (terminus_2.py _limit_output_length; present in 161/445 Terminus2__Claude-Opus-4.6 trajectories). Claude Code spills large results to tool-results/*.txt, which were not downloaded.
corpora.error_markers: Claude Code tool_result.is_error and toolUseResult.stderr/interrupted; Gemini 'Exit Code: N' in output plus toolCall.status; result.json exception_info (5,398 trials) and exception.txt. Terminus has no exit-code field, only terminal text.
corpora.provider_request_ids: YES for one submission: WozCode__Claude-Opus-4.6 Anthropic requestId on 444/444 sessions, 7,272 distinct, 12,327 entries, 12,327 decode v7, 12,279 agree within [-2 s, +600 s]. OpenAI Responses resp_ ids in hookele (12,804, 1 s clock, 12,804/12,804 bracketed by harness ts +-1 s). NOT present in ClaudeCode__GLM-4.7 (GLM endpoint, 0 ids) or cchuter (local MiniMax gguf, 0 ids). Gemini responseId/headers are absent from gemini-cli logs.
corpora.notes: Best multi-harness public corpus found in this group: 21 ATIF-bearing agent harnesses plus 3 native formats, about 20 model families, the same 89 tasks x 5 trials each. That suits the N6 cross-harness transfer matrix. Threat-model caveat: Terminus step clocks are host-side harness clocks. Claude Code, Gemini-CLI and hookele logs are written by the agent CLI inside the sandbox and copied out, which is weaker under execution-path compromise.

prior_art_internal_embodiment.claim: Witness-free structural checking of call/result records (join integrity) as part of fabrication detection
prior_art_internal_embodiment.closest_existing_work: Harbor ATIF Pydantic models (harbor-framework/harbor @3e30cca0, src/harbor/models/trajectories/trajectory.py and step.py), applied whenever a trajectory is built, loaded or validated (src/harbor/utils/trajectory_validator.py)
prior_art_internal_embodiment.what_it_does: Raises an error if an observation result's source_call_id is not in the same step's tool_calls ids; requires sequential step_ids from 1; requires every timestamp to parse as ISO-8601; requires unique ids for embedded subagent trajectories.
prior_art_internal_embodiment.what_it_does_not_do: No timestamp monotonicity or ordering check (567 published ATIF files are non-monotonic and pass). Results without a source_call_id are allowed. No check of result content against anything (repeats, sizes, grammar, state). No timing or duration check. No provider-id clock. It validates format, not truth.
prior_art_internal_embodiment.verdict_reasoning: Referential call/result integrity as a schema check is TAKEN (Harbor embodies it). Our contribution can only be the content-, time- and state-level checks layered on top, which Harbor does not do.
prior_art_internal_embodiment.deciding_citation: trajectory.py validate_tool_call_references: docstring 'Validate that observation source_call_ids reference valid tool_call_ids.' raising ValueError when 'source_call_id ... is not found in step {step_id}'s tool_calls'. URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-framework/harbor/3e30cca047a4d0dc1fb209bf5a74ff761b794b90/src/harbor/models/trajectories/trajectory.py

prior_art_internal_embodiment.claim: N1 / N3: harness-measured durations (LLM time vs execution time) used as a fabrication signal
prior_art_internal_embodiment.closest_existing_work: Harbor Terminus-2 agent (src/harbor/agents/terminus_2/terminus_2.py) records api_request_times_msec, one time.time() wall time per LLM call, and stamps each ATIF step with datetime.now() after the step's commands run. The tbench.ai leaderboard reports avg_trial_duration.
prior_art_internal_embodiment.what_it_does: Collects per-LLM-request latency and per-step wall-clock and emits them into result.json metadata and ATIF.
prior_art_internal_embodiment.what_it_does_not_do: Nothing in terminus_2.py consumes them beyond appending and emitting (ll. 784, 1134, 1201, 1772). Leaderboard integrity relies on static checks plus an LLM agent judge. No duration-vs-workload or reaction-time check. Other Harbor modules that might read the field were not searched (GitHub code search needs auth).
prior_art_internal_embodiment.verdict: NOVEL (relative to this source group; literature-wide status is decided in B1)
prior_art_internal_embodiment.verdict_reasoning: The timers exist as data and serve as an enabler, not prior art.
prior_art_internal_embodiment.deciding_citation: terminus_2.py ll.1127-1134: 'start_time = time.time()' / 'llm_response = await chat.chat(' / 'request_time_ms = (end_time - start_time) * 1000' / 'self._api_request_times.append(request_time_ms)'; https://www.tbench.ai/news/leaderboard-integrity-update: 'To detect reward hacking, we will run an agent judge over all passing trials in a submission.'

prior_art_internal_embodiment.claim: B2: provider-minted id embeds a clock usable to bracket a stream

implications_for_design: B4 request-ID column: add 'tb2_leaderboard/WozCode (Anthropic, 444 sessions)' and 'tb2_leaderboard/hookele (OpenAI resp_, 443 trials, 1 s)'. The public count of corpora carrying provider ids goes from 1 to 2, or 3 counting the OpenAI 1 s clock. Still one harness (Claude Code) for Anthropic ids.

N6 transfer matrix: the TB2 subset alone spans about 24 harness formats on the same 89 tasks; that is the cleanest cross-harness control available. Add a Harbor/ATIF loader plus 3 native loaders (Claude Code JSONL already exists for swechat/cc_local; Gemini-CLI; hookele).

N1/N3: Terminus-family trials give harness-side api_request_times_msec aligned with host step timestamps (4,876 trials, 146,857 requests) and agent-chosen command waits (arguments.duration). The residual exec time = (ts[n]-ts[n-1]) - api_time[n] - chosen wait is computable without a model. Caveat: duration is model-chosen, so 'execution time' is partly agent-controlled.

Second clock witness: asciinema casts (1,332 + 86) record terminal output events with their own timestamps. Cross-checking cast output against ATIF observation text and step times is a new external-witness-style check on existing records. Whether asciinema runs inside the sandbox (agent-reachable) is UNVERIFIED.
Loader caveat: never let git or the OS rewrite line endings in corpus files (core.autocrlf). Byte counts and hashes of tool output depend on it.
